report.summary: Both failures come from one product bug: the server accepts a year one past the current year. The validator at app/main.py:83 uses `this_year + 1` as the upper bound, but its own error message and both tests expect the current year to be the maximum. Fix the bound in validate_book first; both tests should then pass without changes.

causes.title: Year validation accepts next year, contrary to the documented rule
causes.explanation: validate_book() rejects years outside 1..this_year+1, but the error message it raises says 'Year must be between 1 and {this_year}'. The API test and UI test both expect a year of current_year+1 to be rejected with 'Year must be between'. The app instead returns 201 and stores the book, so the API test sees 201 instead of 422, and the UI never renders the error element because no error is raised. The UI snapshot shows the row 'Future-... Someone 2027' was saved. The behavior is deterministic (no timing involved), so this is a real bug in the application rather than a flaky test. The test expectations match the message text, so the test is right.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:66: assert 201 == 422 (api.create_book(title='T', author='A', year=2027) returned Response [201 Created])
app/main.py:84: raise HTTPException(422, f"Year must be between 1 and {this_year}")
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:44: expect(books.error).to_contain_text("Year must be between") -> 'element(s) not found'
UI aria snapshot shows row "Future-5856a016 Someone 2027 Delete" was created, so the save succeeded
app/main.py:154 and app/main.py:330: insert_book() calls validate_book(), so both the API and form paths use this bound
causes.suggested_fix: Change the check in app/main.py:83 to `if not 1 <= book.year <= this_year:` so it matches the error message and the tests. Before merging, confirm with the product owner that current-year-only is the intended rule. If next year really should be allowed, change the message and the tests instead. Also check update_book (app/main.py:212), which shares validate_book, for the same behavior.
